summary: Production EKS pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff after deployment
description: After the latest deployment to the payments namespace, 3 pods entered CrashLoopBackOff. Logs show OOMKilled events. Memory limits appear too low for the new image version.
resolution: Increased memory requests/limits in the deployment manifest from 256Mi to 512Mi and rolled out a new revision. Root cause was a memory leak introduced in v2.3.1 of the payments service, later patched.
resolution_steps: Check pod events with kubectl describe pod to confirm OOMKilled
Review recent image/tag changes in the deployment
Temporarily bump memory limits and re-deploy to restore service
File a problem ticket against the service owner for the memory leak
Validate with Prometheus/Grafana memory graphs post-fix

summary: JWT token validation failing intermittently on auth service
description: Users reported random 401 errors. Investigation showed clock skew between auth pods causing JWT 'nbf' validation to fail intermittently.
resolution: Enabled NTP sync (chrony) on all EKS worker nodes and added a 30s leeway to JWT validation to tolerate minor clock drift.
resolution_steps: Reproduce by checking auth service logs for 'token not yet valid' errors
Compare system clocks across worker nodes
Enable/verify NTP (chrony) service on nodes
Add clock-skew leeway in JWT validation config
Monitor 401 rate for 24h post-fix

summary: GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline failing at Docker Hub push step
description: The 'main' branch pipeline failed at docker push with 'unauthorized: authentication required'. Personal Access Token used in the workflow secret had expired.
resolution: Rotated the Docker Hub Personal Access Token, updated the GitHub Actions repository secret DOCKERHUB_TOKEN, and re-ran the pipeline.
resolution_steps: Check workflow logs for the exact auth error
Confirm token expiry in Docker Hub account settings
Generate a new Personal Access Token scoped to read/write
Update the GitHub repo secret
Re-run the failed workflow

summary: Jira Service Management automation rule not creating linked sub-tasks
description: The ART Team Automation Flow was not creating sub-tasks for incidents raised via the Incident Clone Portal. Smart value used in the automation referenced a custom field not available on the destination project.
resolution: Corrected the smart value reference to use the shared field, and added a fallback branch in the automation rule for when the field is empty. Escalated to Atlassian admin to align field configuration across projects.
resolution_steps: Open Automation > Audit log to check the failed rule execution
Identify the smart value or field causing the null reference
Confirm field availability/mapping across both request types
Update rule logic and add error-handling branch
Re-test with a sample ticket before closing

summary: Send Web Request action returning 404 in JSM automation
description: An automation rule using 'Send Web Request' to notify an external Teams channel returned HTTP 404. Webhook URL had been regenerated after a Teams workspace change.
resolution: Regenerated and updated the Teams incoming webhook URL in the automation rule's Send Web Request action, then validated with a test trigger.
resolution_steps: Reproduce and capture the exact response code/body from the audit log
Verify the webhook URL is still valid in Teams connector settings
Update the URL in the automation action
Trigger a test rule execution
Confirm delivery in the Teams channel

summary: Cascading dropdown showing empty child field with no way to hide it
description: In the Incident Clone Portal request form, the sub-team cascading dropdown shows an empty child selector when a parent team has no configured children, confusing end users.
resolution: No fix available yet; this is a known JSM UI limitation. Workaround is to add a placeholder 'N/A' child option for parent teams without sub-teams. Escalated to manager for a permanent fix or Atlassian feature request.
resolution_steps: Confirm which parent teams are affected
Add an 'N/A' placeholder child value as an interim workaround
Document the limitation for end users
Track as a longer-term backlog item with the platform admin

summary: Prometheus alert: high pod restart count on monitoring namespace
description: Grafana dashboard flagged repeated restarts for the kube-prometheus-stack Alertmanager pod after a Helm upgrade.
resolution: Rolled back the Helm release to the previous chart version due to an incompatible values.yaml schema change, then re-applied the upgrade incrementally with validated config.
resolution_steps: Check kubectl get pods -n monitoring for restart counts
Review Helm release history: helm history kube-prometheus-stack
Roll back with helm rollback if a recent upgrade is the cause
Validate values.yaml against the new chart's schema before retrying
Confirm dashboards return to green

summary: Rolling update stuck at 50% availability during EKS deployment
description: A deployment rollout for the inventory service stalled with 2 of 4 pods unavailable, due to pod anti-affinity rules unable to be satisfied on the current node group.
resolution: Temporarily scaled the node group to add capacity, then tuned maxUnavailable/maxSurge in the rolling update strategy to reduce pressure on anti-affinity placement.
resolution_steps: kubectl rollout status to confirm the stuck state
kubectl describe pod for scheduling/anti-affinity failures
Scale the EKS node group or adjust affinity rules
Tune maxUnavailable/maxSurge in the deployment strategy
Re-trigger rollout and confirm 100% availability

summary: Kubernetes Secret not being picked up by pod after rotation
description: A rotated database credential Secret did not take effect; pods continued using the old credential and failed DB connections.
resolution: Secrets mounted as environment variables require a pod restart to pick up new values. Performed a rolling restart of the deployment after Secret rotation and documented this as a required step in the runbook.
resolution_steps: Confirm the Secret was updated: kubectl get secret -o yaml
Check if the Secret is mounted as env var (requires restart) vs volume (auto-updates)
Perform kubectl rollout restart deployment
Verify new DB connections succeed
Update runbook to include restart step post-rotation

summary: VS Code Remote-SSH connection to EC2 control server timing out
description: Engineer could not connect via Remote-SSH from the office network; connection timed out on port 22.
resolution: Office network blocks outbound port 22. Switched to Git Bash with an SSH config using a non-standard port forwarded through a bastion, and documented the workaround for other engineers on restricted networks.
resolution_steps: Confirm whether port 22 is blocked outbound (telnet test)
Use an alternate port or SSH-over-HTTPS tunnel if available
Configure Git Bash / SSH config with the workaround
Test connection and document the fix for the team

summary: Terraform apply fails with 'command not found' on Windows
description: terraform apply failed immediately with 'terraform' not recognized as a command, despite the binary being downloaded.
resolution: The Terraform binary directory was not added to the Windows PATH environment variable. Added it via System Properties > Environment Variables and confirmed with 'terraform -version' in a new terminal.
resolution_steps: Confirm terraform.exe location on disk
Add the folder to the Windows PATH system variable
Open a new terminal session (PATH changes don't apply to open ones)
Verify with terraform -version

summary: Incident ticket stuck in 'Waiting for Support' with no automation trigger
description: A ticket raised through the Incident Clone Portal did not trigger the ART Team Automation Flow, leaving it unassigned for several hours.
resolution: Root cause was a mismatch between the portal's request type and the automation rule's trigger condition (the rule only fired for one of two valid request types). Broadened the trigger condition to cover both request types.
resolution_steps: Check which request type the ticket was raised under
Compare against the automation rule's trigger/condition JQL
Broaden or correct the trigger condition
Re-test with sample tickets from each request type
Monitor next 10 incoming tickets for correct routing

summary: No admin access blocking custom field creation for new request type
description: Team needed a new custom field on a request type to support a new automation flow, but the engineer lacked Jira admin permissions to create it.
resolution: Raised an escalation ticket to the Atlassian admin (Divij) with the exact field spec and request type. Field was created and linked within 1 business day. Documented the admin escalation process for future field requests.
resolution_steps: Draft the exact field name, type, and target request type
Raise an escalation ticket to the Atlassian project admin
Await field creation and confirm mapping to the automation rule
Test end-to-end before communicating availability to the team

summary: Docker build fails on GitHub Actions with 'no space left on device'
description: The staging pipeline's docker build step failed with disk space errors after several consecutive builds on the same self-hosted runner.
resolution: Added a 'docker system prune -af' cleanup step at the start of the workflow and enabled build cache pruning to prevent disk exhaustion on the runner.
resolution_steps: Check runner disk usage with df -h
Identify dangling images/build cache as the cause
Add a docker system prune step to the workflow
Re-run the pipeline and confirm successful build
Add periodic scheduled cleanup for the runner

summary: Flask-based internal service returning 500 due to unhandled JWT decode error
description: An internal Python Flask microservice crashed requests with HTTP 500 when receiving a malformed JWT, instead of returning a clean 401.
resolution: Wrapped the JWT decode call in a try/except for jwt.exceptions.InvalidTokenError and returned a structured 401 response. Added a regression test for malformed tokens.
resolution_steps: Reproduce with a deliberately malformed token
Check application logs/stack trace for the unhandled exception
Add exception handling around token decode
Return appropriate 401 with a clear error body
Add automated test coverage for this case

summary: Multi-container pod: sidecar container failing readiness probe
description: A pod with a logging sidecar container was marked NotReady because the sidecar's readiness probe path returned 404, blocking traffic to the healthy main container.
resolution: Corrected the readiness probe path in the sidecar container spec to match the actual health endpoint, and split readiness so the main container's traffic isn't gated by an unrelated sidecar.
resolution_steps: kubectl describe pod to identify which container is failing probes
Check the configured probe path/port against the container's actual endpoint
Correct the probe configuration
Consider decoupling unrelated sidecar health from main traffic readiness
Confirm pod reaches Ready state

summary: Teams notification not received for P1 incident despite automation success
description: Automation audit log showed the rule executed successfully, but the on-call engineer did not receive the Teams alert for a P1 incident.
resolution: The Teams channel the webhook posted to had been archived after a reorg. Updated the automation to point to the correct active channel and added a secondary email notification as a fallback for P1 incidents.
resolution_steps: Confirm rule execution success in the audit log
Check destination channel/webhook validity
Update to the correct active channel
Add a fallback notification channel for P1 severity
Send a test P1-severity trigger to confirm delivery

summary: EC2 instance unreachable after security group change
description: A control server became unreachable via SSH after a security group update removed the inbound rule for the office IP range.
resolution: Restored the inbound rule for the correct office IP CIDR in the security group, and added a change-management note requiring review before security group edits on shared control servers.
resolution_steps: Confirm reachability failure is network-level (not instance/OS)
Check recent security group changes in CloudTrail
Restore or correct the inbound rule
Test SSH connectivity
Document a change-review step for future SG edits

summary: Helm upgrade for kube-prometheus-stack breaks existing Grafana dashboards
description: After upgrading the kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart, several custom Grafana dashboards disappeared because they were not stored as ConfigMaps and were lost on pod recreation.
resolution: Re-created the dashboards and this time provisioned them as ConfigMaps with the grafana_dashboard label so they persist across chart upgrades and pod restarts.
resolution_steps: Confirm dashboards are missing post-upgrade, not just misconfigured
Check whether dashboards were provisioned via ConfigMap or manually created in-UI
Re-create dashboards as version-controlled ConfigMaps
Apply the grafana_dashboard sidecar label for auto-discovery
Verify persistence after a test pod restart

summary: Duplicate incident tickets created for the same outage
description: Three separate JSM tickets were raised by different users for the same production outage, causing duplicate on-call paging and confusing status updates.
resolution: Linked the duplicate tickets to a single parent incident, closed the duplicates with a reference note, and communicated a single status update thread. Recommended a 'possible duplicate' automation check based on similar summary/category within a time window as a future enhancement.
resolution_steps: Identify all tickets referencing the same outage window/service
Designate one as the parent incident
Link/close duplicates with a reference to the parent
Post one consolidated status update
Log as a process improvement item for future automation

summary: SLA breach warning for P2 tickets not escalating to team lead
description: P2 incidents nearing SLA breach were not triggering the expected escalation notification to the team lead, only to the original assignee.
resolution: Automation rule's escalation branch referenced the wrong field for 'team lead' lookup. Corrected the field mapping and added an additional test case for SLA breach simulation.
resolution_steps: Reproduce by simulating a near-breach ticket in a test project
Check audit log for the escalation branch execution
Correct the team lead field reference
Re-test with simulated SLA timers
Confirm escalation notification reaches the team lead
